about: Buildings measured by hand. Each replaces any Ordnance Survey outline it overlaps. Parts are rectangles in metres in a local grid: origin (E, N) on the British National Grid, u along `bearing` (degrees clockwise from grid north), w at right angles to the left of u. Heights are metres above the ground: `eaves` where the roof starts, `top` the ridge. Roof types: gable (ridge runs `along` u or w), lean (falls towards the `low` side: u0, u1, w0 or w1), hip. `door` is the side the main door faces (n = +w, s = -w, e = +u, w = -u). Materials: see MATERIALS in js/buildings.js. `details` record what was seen of a building (matched by the point `at`, lat/lon, inside its outline): wall/roof/groundWall/plinth materials, `front` (compass side facing the road, letter or degrees), `doors` and `chimneys` as fractions 0..1 left to right as seen from the front (chimneys along the main ridge), `blank` compass sides seen to have no windows or doors, `windows` [ground, upper] counts on the front (or, for either floor, a list of fractions placing each window, or null where that floor couldn't be seen), `storeys`, `label`. `roads` entries with `osm` (an OpenStreetMap way id) set `sidewalk` (both/left/right/no, sides relative to the way's direction) where OSM has no sidewalk tag. `gates` are gateways in walls seen in Street View (`at`, the compass `face` out of the enclosure, opening `width` in metres). `grounds` surfaces are clear of hedges. `church` gives St Bartholomew's tower, nave, aisles, chancel and porch measured from the LIDAR (u, w ranges; eaves and top in metres). `lidarBuildings` are garages and sheds that the Ordnance Survey outlines miss: each `at` point picks a building-shaped blob of the LIDAR, confirmed on an aerial photograph, which tools/fit_buildings.py measures like any other building.

buildings.name: Old Hall Cottage
buildings.label: Old Hall Cottage
buildings.notes: Grade II, early 19th-century estate cottage. Two storeys of red brick under a hipped pantile roof with a central stack, single-storey lean-to wings either side. The front (to Newark Road) has two white sashes per floor and blind recesses in the middle, and no door.
buildings.sources: Historic England listing (via Wikipedia); EA LIDAR 2022 last return and intensity; Street View from Newark Road, checked 2026-10-15

buildings.sources: aerial photographs (Google, imagery 2026, its lean of 0.4 m north per metre of height measured on the church tower; Bing) and Street View from Newark Road (May 2025), measured 2026-10-16

buildings.name: House and pantiled ranges round a yard, Newark Road
buildings.notes: The fitter had turned the west range into a lean-to and the north range into flat blocks. Read from the LIDAR by hand: a single-storey west range and a taller range across the north (solar panels on its south slope, a stack on its east gable), stepping down to a long low range that runs to the road with a small stack near its west end; across the yard a two-storey slate-roofed house, hipped at both ends, with a gabled wing to the yard whose end has a garage door and a window above. The house's end to the road is blank brick behind a brick wall. The tall 'block' north-west of the north range in the LIDAR is a tree (high intensity, foliage on the aerial).
buildings.sources: EA LIDAR 2022 last return and intensity (read with tools/survey_grid.py); aerial photograph (Google, imagery 2026); Street View from Newark Road (imagery as served 2026-10-16); measured 2026-10-16

buildings.name: Tall slate-roofed house among trees west of Newark Road
buildings.notes: Hidden from the roads by trees, so only its roof is known. It stands inside an OpenStreetMap farmyard, which had made it a windowless barn, and the fitter had broken it into lean-tos. Read from the LIDAR by hand: a tall block with a steep roof running north-south (ridge 10.5 m), a lower hipped block to the east, and a west wing whose gable roof sweeps down westwards in a catslide to a flat-roofed end; a low shed to the south-west. Slate throughout (low laser intensity). Walls, doors and windows unseen.
buildings.sources: EA LIDAR 2022 last return and intensity (read with tools/survey_grid.py); aerial photograph (Google, imagery 2026); measured 2026-10-16

buildings.name: Shed south-west of the tall house among trees
buildings.notes: Low pitched-roof shed, from the LIDAR (2.2 m eaves, 3.1 m ridge); unseen from the roads.
buildings.sources: EA LIDAR 2022 last return (read with tools/survey_grid.py), measured 2026-10-16

buildings.name: Two staggered ranges at the south-west end of the yards behind Newark Road
buildings.notes: The fitter had run one long flat roof down the middle of both. Read from the LIDAR by hand: a pantiled range to the south and a brown-tiled range to the north set a few metres east, joined by a flat-roofed link, with solar panels on the north range's east slope and a light-roofed lean-to (a conservatory, by its colour on the aerial) along its west side. Unseen from the roads.
buildings.sources: EA LIDAR 2022 last return and intensity (read with tools/survey_grid.py); aerial photograph (Google, imagery 2026); measured 2026-10-16

church.name: St Bartholomew's Church
church.notes: West tower with a panelled parapet and corner pinnacles; nave with a clerestory under a low-pitched roof; lean-to aisles both sides; chancel with a near-flat roof and pinnacles on the east gable; south porch; a flat-roofed boiler house in the angle of the tower and the north aisle. Doors and windows are those the listing describes, spaced evenly along each wall. Each part's outline is where the LIDAR height crosses half way between the part and what is next to it (sampled every 0.5 m along and across the church), so roofs include their eaves.
church.sources: EA LIDAR 2022 last return (1 m); Historic England listing; clock on the west face from the Southwell & Nottingham Church History Project
